title: Signature Math Mapping — ASCII Text
description: How the Signature bitstring reads as ASCII Text (Text encodings). ASCII is the 7-bit American Standard Code for Information Interchange: 128 code points (0-127); printable characters start at 32. One byte per character.

fields.name: ASCII Text
fields.system: ASCII is the 7-bit American Standard Code for Information Interchange: 128 code points (0-127); printable characters start at 32. One byte per character.
fields.mapping: Take the Signature bitstring in 7-bit groups; each group is one ASCII code point. The Signature's text labels (e.g. 'SIGNATURE-ONE') also encode directly to their ASCII bytes, so the mark travels as plain text.
apply: 1. Reduce the Signature to its 144-bit string on the 12x12 grid (1 = geometry present, 0 = null).
2. Split the bitstring into 7-bit groups from the left; pad the last group with trailing zeros.
3. Convert each group to decimal (0-127) and look up the ASCII character.
4. The resulting character string is the ASCII form of the Signature.
